significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) law: a reproducible ordering—“factual → most localized/MLP-driven/mid-layer; conceptual and relational → more distributed/attention-driven; procedural → latest-layer, serial”—whose localization measurements predict editability, paraphrase robustness, and stored-but-unretrieved failures. This would establish both a mechanistic decomposition of knowledge retrieval and a behavioral predictive coupling; it would constrain where mechanisms and editing effects should appear for each knowledge type, addressing the localization–editability dissociation examined by Hase et al., “Does Localization Inform Editing?” (NeurIPS 2023), rather than merely identifying another decodable representation. Verified false across the asserted types and model families would rule out knowledge type as a stable organizing variable for localization and undermine the proposed unified explanation, although the bundled ordering and correlations could fail separately, making the negative branch less decisive. After topic substitution, the score falls materially because the generic topic suggests studying localization and retrieval, whereas the specific cross-type ordering and three downstream couplings are false of the median proposal on this topic.

reach.justification: The claim hands downstream users explicit handles: “LocalizationScore,” the “MLP-vs-attention reliance ratio,” “PeakLayerDepth,” and “MechanismParaphraseInvariance,” with the spectrum intended to predict “where editing works” and “when stored knowledge fails to surface.” These are potentially ex-ante auditing and intervention handles because their measured position is claimed to forecast edit success and retrieval-gap risk before a new edit or query outcome, rather than merely explain an observed failure. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a cross-family ordering and coupling—the claim calls the spectrum “reproducible” and connects it to editing and retrieval reliability—so researchers and model auditors would know what relation to expect rather than receiving only a search procedure, though no concrete deployment gate or outside-AI uptake is specified. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the broad knowledge-representation topic alone supplies neither these named metrics nor the asserted cross-type predictive relation.
